metadata.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift

nodes.name: Internal Covariate Shift
nodes.statement: The change in the distribution of network activations due to the change in network parameters during training.
nodes.statement_clean: Drift in the distribution of inner-layer inputs as upstream parameters update during training.

nodes.name: Covariate Shift
nodes.statement: A change in the input distribution to a learning system, typically handled via domain adaptation.

nodes.name: Whitening
nodes.statement: A linear transformation of inputs to have zero mean, unit variance, and decorrelated coordinates; known to speed up convergence.

nodes.name: Normalization Transform $\Norm(\vx, \setX)$
nodes.statement: $\widehat{\mathrm{x}} = \Norm(\mathrm{x}, \setX)$ denoting a normalization that depends on the example $\mathrm{x}$ and on the full set $\setX$ of training inputs; backpropagation must include $\partial \Norm/\partial \setX$ to avoid blow-up.

nodes.name: Per-dimension Normalization
nodes.statement: For a $d$-dimensional input $\vx = (x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(d)})$, normalize each coordinate independently as $\widehat{x}^{(k)} = \frac{x^{(k)} - \E[x^{(k)}]}{\sqrt{\Var[x^{(k)}]}}$.

nodes.name: Affine Restoration $y^{(k)} = \gamma^{(k)} \widehat{x}^{(k)} + \beta^{(k)}$
nodes.statement: Per-activation learnable scale $\gamma^{(k)}$ and shift $\beta^{(k)}$ applied after normalization so the transform can represent the identity (recovered by $\gamma^{(k)} = \sqrt{\Var[x^{(k)}]}$, $\beta^{(k)} = \E[x^{(k)}]$).

nodes.name: Batch Normalizing Transform $\BatchNorm_{\gamma,\beta}$
nodes.statement: The mapping $\BatchNorm_{\gamma,\beta}: x_{1\ldots m} \to y_{1\ldots m}$ that normalizes a single activation across a mini-batch $\setB = \{x_{1\ldots m}\}$ and then applies the affine restoration $y_i = \gamma \widehat{x}_i + \beta$.

nodes.name: Convolutional BN
nodes.statement: For a feature map of size $p \times q$ over a mini-batch of size $m$, jointly normalize all $m' = m \cdot p\, q$ activations and learn a single $(\gamma^{(k)}, \beta^{(k)})$ pair per feature map.

nodes.name: Inference Normalization with Population Statistics
nodes.statement: At inference, replace mini-batch statistics with population estimates: $\widehat{x} = \frac{x - \E[x]}{\sqrt{\Var[x] + \epsilon}}$ using the unbiased variance $\Var[x] = \frac{m}{m-1} \E_\setB[\sigma_\setB^2]$.

nodes.name: SGD Loss Minimization
nodes.statement: $\Theta = \arg\min_\Theta \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \ell(\mathrm{x}_i, \Theta)$ where the loss over the training set $\mathrm{x}_{1\ldots N}$ is minimized over network parameters $\Theta$.

nodes.name: Differentiable Whitening that Accounts for $\Theta$
nodes.statement: Find a normalization $\widehat{\vx} = \Norm(\vx, \setX)$ that (i) depends on $\Theta$ in a differentiable way and (ii) does not require reanalyzing the entire training set $\setX$ after every parameter update.

nodes.name: Batch Normalizing Transform
nodes.statement: Computes $\BN{x_i}{\gamma,\beta}$ for each activation $x_i$ in a mini-batch by subtracting the mini-batch mean, dividing by $\sqrt{\sigma_\setB^2 + \epsilon}$, and applying the learned affine $\gamma\widehat{x}_i + \beta$.
input: Values of $x$ over a mini-batch: $\setB = \{x_{1\ldots m}\}$

nodes.name: Training a Batch-Normalized Network
nodes.statement: Wraps a network $\norig$ by inserting a BN transform before each chosen activation, trains the augmented parameters, then freezes the BN transforms with population statistics for inference.
nodes.pseudocode: Build $\ntrain$ by adding $y^{(k)} = \BN{x^{(k)}}{\gamma^{(k)},\beta^{(k)}}$ for each $k$; train on $\Theta \cup \{\gamma^{(k)},\beta^{(k)}\}$; for inference, set $\E[x] \leftarrow \E_\setB[\mu_\setB]$, $\Var[x] \leftarrow \frac{m}{m-1} \E_\setB[\sigma_\setB^2]$; replace each BN with the linear transform $y = \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{\Var[x]+\epsilon}} x + \big(\beta - \frac{\gamma\,\E[x]}{\sqrt{\Var[x]+\epsilon}}\big)$.

nodes.name: BN Backprop Chain Rule
nodes.statement: $\partial \ell / \partial \widehat{x}_i = (\partial \ell/\partial y_i)\gamma$; $\partial \ell/\partial \sigma_\setB^2 = \sum_i (\partial \ell/\partial \widehat{x}_i)(x_i - \mu_\setB)\,\frac{-1}{2}(\sigma_\setB^2 + \epsilon)^{-3/2}$; $\partial \ell/\partial \mu_\setB$, $\partial \ell/\partial x_i$, $\partial \ell/\partial \gamma = \sum_i (\partial \ell/\partial y_i)\widehat{x}_i$, $\partial \ell/\partial \beta = \sum_i \partial \ell/\partial y_i$.

nodes.name: Scale-Invariance Identity for BN
nodes.statement: $\BatchNorm(W \vu) = \BatchNorm((aW)\vu)$ for any scalar $a$, with derivative $\partial \BatchNorm((aW)\vu)/\partial \vu = \partial \BatchNorm(W\vu)/\partial \vu$ and $\partial \BatchNorm((aW)\vu)/\partial(aW) = \frac{1}{a}\,\partial \BatchNorm(W\vu)/\partial W$.

nodes.name: Identity Recoverable by BN
nodes.statement: By choosing $\gamma^{(k)} = \sqrt{\Var[x^{(k)}]}$ and $\beta^{(k)} = \E[x^{(k)}]$, the BN transform recovers the original (unnormalized) activations, so it can represent the identity transformation.

nodes.name: Zero Mean / Unit Variance of $\widehat{x}$
nodes.statement: The normalized values satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^m \widehat{x}_i = 0$ and $\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m \widehat{x}_i^2 = 1$, so each $\widehat{x}^{(k)}$ has expected mean $0$ and variance $1$ (neglecting $\epsilon$) when mini-batch elements are i.i.d.
assumptions: Mini-batch elements sampled from the same distribution

nodes.name: BN is Invariant to Weight Rescaling
nodes.statement: BatchNorm is invariant to a scalar rescaling $W \mapsto aW$ of layer weights, so the layer Jacobian (and gradient with respect to the input) is unaffected by the parameter scale, while the gradient with respect to $W$ scales by $1/a$.

nodes.name: Singular Values of Layer Jacobians Near 1
nodes.statement: Batch Normalization may lead the layer Jacobians to have singular values close to 1, which is known to be beneficial for training; under a Gaussian/uncorrelated linearization $\vzhat = J \vxhat$, $JJ^T = I$.
conclusions: $JJ^T = I$, hence all singular values of $J$ equal $1$

nodes.name: Bias Subsumed by $\beta$
nodes.statement: Since BN subtracts the mean of $W\vu + \vb$, the bias $\vb$ is canceled and its role is absorbed by $\beta$; the layer becomes $\vz = g(\BatchNorm(W\vu))$.

nodes.name: BN as Regularizer
nodes.statement: Because each example is normalized in conjunction with the rest of its mini-batch, the network output is no longer deterministic for a given input, which empirically improves generalization and lets Dropout be reduced or removed.

nodes.name: Per-dimension Variances Avoid Singular Covariance
nodes.statement: Mini-batch use is enabled by per-dimension variances rather than joint covariances; jointly whitening would require regularization since the mini-batch size is typically smaller than the number of activations.

nodes.name: Comparison to Standardization Layer
nodes.statement: BN resembles the standardization layer of Gulcehre and Bengio but applies before the nonlinearity, learns a scale/shift to recover identity, handles convolutional layers, and gives deterministic inference.

nodes.name: Naive Mean-Subtraction Bias Blow-up
nodes.statement: If $\widehat{x} = x - \E[x]$ with $x = u + b$ and the gradient step ignores $\partial \E[x]/\partial b$, then $b \leftarrow b + \Delta b$ leaves the layer output unchanged, so $b$ grows indefinitely while the loss stays fixed.

nodes.name: MNIST Sigmoid Network with BN
nodes.statement: A 3-hidden-layer (100 sigmoid units) network on MNIST trained for 50000 steps with mini-batches of 60: BN improves test accuracy and yields more stable input distributions to the sigmoid (Fig. 1).

nodes.name: ImageNet Inception with BN
nodes.statement: BN applied to a $13.6 \cdot 10^6$-parameter Inception variant on LSVRC2012; BN-Baseline matches Inception in less than half the steps, BN-x5 reaches 72.2\% accuracy in 14$\times$ fewer steps, BN-x30 reaches 74.8\%, BN-x5-Sigmoid reaches 69.8\%.

nodes.name: BN-Inception Ensemble on ImageNet
nodes.statement: An ensemble of 6 networks based on BN-x30 reaches top-5 validation error 4.9\% (test error 4.82\%), exceeding human-rater accuracy and the prior best results.

nodes.name: Derivation of BN Backprop
nodes.statement: Apply the chain rule to $\BatchNorm_{\gamma,\beta}$ accounting for the dependence of $\widehat{x}_i$ on $\mu_\setB$ and $\sigma_\setB^2$, both of which depend on every $x_j$ in the mini-batch.

nodes.name: Identity-Recoverability Argument
nodes.statement: Substitute $\gamma^{(k)} = \sqrt{\Var[x^{(k)}]}$ and $\beta^{(k)} = \E[x^{(k)}]$ into $y^{(k)} = \gamma^{(k)} \widehat{x}^{(k)} + \beta^{(k)}$ and use $\widehat{x}^{(k)} = (x^{(k)} - \E[x^{(k)}])/\sqrt{\Var[x^{(k)}]}$ to recover $y^{(k)} = x^{(k)}$.

nodes.name: Scale-Invariance Derivation
nodes.statement: Mini-batch mean and variance of $aW\vu$ scale by $a$ and $a^2$, so the standardized $\widehat{x}$ is unchanged; differentiate to obtain the Jacobian identities.

nodes.name: Singular-Values-Near-1 Argument
nodes.statement: Under Gaussian, uncorrelated $\vxhat, \vzhat$ with $\vzhat = J \vxhat$, both have unit covariance, hence $I = \Cov[\vzhat] = J \Cov[\vxhat] J^T = J J^T$.

nodes.name: Differentiate $y_i$ in $\widehat{x}_i$
nodes.statement: From $y_i = \gamma \widehat{x}_i + \beta$, $\partial \ell/\partial \widehat{x}_i = (\partial \ell/\partial y_i)\,\gamma$.

nodes.name: Differentiate w.r.t. $\sigma_\setB^2$
nodes.statement: $\partial \ell/\partial \sigma_\setB^2 = \sum_i (\partial \ell/\partial \widehat{x}_i)\,(x_i - \mu_\setB)\,\frac{-1}{2}(\sigma_\setB^2 + \epsilon)^{-3/2}$.

nodes.name: Differentiate w.r.t. $\mu_\setB$
nodes.statement: $\partial \ell/\partial \mu_\setB = \big(\sum_i (\partial \ell/\partial \widehat{x}_i)\,\frac{-1}{\sqrt{\sigma_\setB^2 + \epsilon}}\big) + (\partial \ell/\partial \sigma_\setB^2)\,\frac{\sum_i -2(x_i - \mu_\setB)}{m}$.

nodes.name: Combine for $\partial \ell/\partial x_i$
nodes.statement: $\partial \ell/\partial x_i = (\partial \ell/\partial \widehat{x}_i)\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{\sigma_\setB^2 + \epsilon}} + (\partial \ell/\partial \sigma_\setB^2)\,\frac{2(x_i - \mu_\setB)}{m} + (\partial \ell/\partial \mu_\setB)\,\frac{1}{m}$.

nodes.name: Gradients w.r.t. parameters
nodes.statement: $\partial \ell/\partial \gamma = \sum_i (\partial \ell/\partial y_i)\widehat{x}_i$; $\partial \ell/\partial \beta = \sum_i \partial \ell/\partial y_i$.

nodes.name: Mean and variance scale with $a$
nodes.statement: Replacing $W$ by $aW$ scales mini-batch mean of $W\vu$ by $a$ and variance by $a^2$, leaving $\widehat{x}_i = (a\,x_i - a\mu_\setB)/\sqrt{a^2 \sigma_\setB^2 + \epsilon}$ unchanged (modulo $\epsilon$).

nodes.name: Equate BN outputs
nodes.statement: Conclude $\BatchNorm(W\vu) = \BatchNorm((aW)\vu)$.

nodes.name: Differentiate to obtain Jacobian identities
nodes.statement: Differentiate w.r.t. $\vu$ and $aW$ to get $\partial \BatchNorm((aW)\vu)/\partial \vu = \partial \BatchNorm(W\vu)/\partial \vu$ and $\partial \BatchNorm((aW)\vu)/\partial(aW) = (1/a)\,\partial \BatchNorm(W\vu)/\partial W$.

nodes.name: Both vectors have unit covariance
nodes.statement: By assumption $\vxhat$ and $\vzhat$ are Gaussian, uncorrelated, and normalized, so $\Cov[\vxhat] = I$ and $\Cov[\vzhat] = I$.

nodes.name: Apply linearization $\vzhat = J\vxhat$
nodes.statement: Then $\Cov[\vzhat] = J\,\Cov[\vxhat]\,J^T = J J^T$.

nodes.name: Conclude $JJ^T = I$
nodes.statement: Combining, $JJ^T = I$, so all singular values of $J$ equal 1.

nodes.name: Mini-batch mean
nodes.statement: $\mu_\setB \leftarrow \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m x_i$.

nodes.name: Mini-batch variance
nodes.statement: $\sigma_\setB^2 \leftarrow \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m (x_i - \mu_\setB)^2$.

nodes.name: Normalize
nodes.statement: $\widehat{x}_i \leftarrow \frac{x_i - \mu_\setB}{\sqrt{\sigma_\setB^2 + \epsilon}}$.

nodes.name: Scale and shift
nodes.statement: $y_i \leftarrow \gamma \widehat{x}_i + \beta \equiv \BN{x_i}{\gamma,\beta}$.

nodes.name: Initialize training network
nodes.statement: $\ntrain \leftarrow \norig$.

nodes.name: Insert BN before each chosen activation
nodes.statement: For $k = 1,\ldots,K$: add $y^{(k)} = \BN{x^{(k)}}{\gamma^{(k)},\beta^{(k)}}$ to $\ntrain$ and rewire each downstream layer to consume $y^{(k)}$ instead of $x^{(k)}$.

nodes.name: Train augmented parameters
nodes.statement: Train $\ntrain$ to optimize $\Theta \cup \{\gamma^{(k)}, \beta^{(k)}\}_{k=1}^K$.

nodes.name: Initialize inference network
nodes.statement: $\ninf \leftarrow \ntrain$ (BN parameters frozen for inference).

nodes.name: Estimate population statistics
nodes.statement: For each BN, process multiple training mini-batches $\setB$ of size $m$ and average: $\E[x] \leftarrow \E_\setB[\mu_\setB]$ and $\Var[x] \leftarrow \frac{m}{m-1}\E_\setB[\sigma_\setB^2]$.

nodes.name: Replace BN with single linear transform
nodes.statement: In $\ninf$ replace $y = \BN{x}{\gamma,\beta}$ by $y = \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{\Var[x]+\epsilon}}\,x + \big(\beta - \frac{\gamma\,\E[x]}{\sqrt{\Var[x]+\epsilon}}\big)$.
